--- title: "[DuckDBGAM]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} GAM that reads data directly from DuckDB via SQL. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/duckdb.py#L78-L322){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python DuckDBGAM(formula, family=None, *, n_discrete=200, chunk_size=100000) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `DuckDBGAM` is a SQL-native variant of `BigGAM` for fitting a GAM without first loading the source data into pandas or polars. `fit()` accepts either a bare table/view name or an arbitrary `SELECT` query — anything expressible in SQL, including joins, filters, aggregations, and window functions — and DuckDB does the work of producing the resulting rows. Internally, `_stream_as_dict` reads those rows through DuckDB's Arrow batch interface (`conn.sql(query).fetch_arrow_reader(batch_size=chunk_size)`), concatenating `chunk_size`-row Arrow batches into the column-oriented dict that `build_discretized_model_matrix` and `bam_fit` (the same discretized-basis machinery used by `BigGAM`) consume to fit the model. Use `DuckDBGAM` whenever the training data already lives in DuckDB, in Parquet/CSV files DuckDB can scan directly, or in a view/query that would be expensive to materialize by hand before fitting. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [formula]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str or Formula]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Model formula (same syntax as `~whittaker.gam.GAM`), e.g. `"y ~ s(x1) + s(x2)"`. The left-hand side names the response column that must be selectable from `source`; the right-hand side lists smooth terms, linear terms, and interactions in `mgcv`-style syntax. [family]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Family]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Response distribution family, e.g. `Gaussian()`, `Binomial()`, `Poisson()`, or `Gamma()`. Defaults to `Gaussian()` (identity link). [n_discrete]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of discretization grid points per covariate used when building the discretized model matrix (see `build_discretized_model_matrix`). Larger values give a more accurate approximation to the exact basis evaluation at the cost of a larger `grid_size * p` term in memory and compute. Defaults to `200`, which is adequate for most smooths. [chunk_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of rows per Arrow batch fetched from DuckDB while streaming (see `Notes` below). Larger values reduce Python-level batch-processing overhead but increase peak memory per batch; smaller values do the opposite. Defaults to `100_000`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} Memory usage during fitting is bounded by *O(n d + grid_size * p)* rather than *O(n p)*, where *n* is the row count, *d* the number of raw covariates, *p* the number of basis functions, and *grid_size* the discretization resolution (`n_discrete`). The `n d` term comes from streaming the raw columns rather than an *n x p* design matrix; the `grid_size * p` term comes from evaluating the basis only at the discretization grid. `_stream_as_dict` is what keeps the raw data at `O(n d)` rather than materializing a full *n x p* matrix twice as `conn.sql(...).df()` would: it pulls one `chunk_size`-row Arrow batch at a time from `fetch_arrow_reader` and appends each batch's columns to a list, so DuckDB never has to build (and Python never has to hold) more than one batch's worth of Arrow data plus the columns accumulated so far. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#d5efbe71 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import duckdb import numpy as np import whittaker as wt from whittaker.duckdb import DuckDBGAM conn = duckdb.connect() rng = np.random.default_rng(0) conn.execute( "CREATE TABLE data AS " "SELECT i AS id, (i / 100.0) AS x, " "sin(2 * pi() * i / 100.0) + ? * random() AS y " "FROM range(200) AS t(i)", [0.2], ) model = DuckDBGAM("y ~ s(x)").fit("data", conn) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Gaussian(link='identity') Inference: REML Observations: 0 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0970 0.0000 0.000 1 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 8.99 9 30659.670 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 9.99 Scale est: 0.003313 Deviance: 0.6295 Null dev: 102.2248 Dev. expl: 99.4% GCV score: 0.003487 AIC: -564.43 BIC: -531.49 ``` ::: ::: A query can be used directly in place of a table name, e.g. to filter or join before fitting: ::: {#70cbfefc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} model2 = DuckDBGAM("y ~ s(x)").fit_query( "SELECT x, y FROM data WHERE x < 0.8", conn ) print(model2.n_rows) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 80 ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
chunk_size Arrow batch size used when streaming from DuckDB.
n_rows Total number of rows in the DuckDB source used by the most recent fit.
### [chunk_size]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Arrow batch size used when streaming from DuckDB. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [chunk_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} This is the `chunk_size` value passed to `__init__`: the number of rows per Arrow batch that `_stream_as_dict` requests from `conn.sql(query).fetch_arrow_reader(batch_size=...)` while reading `fit()`'s data source. ::: ### [n_rows]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Total number of rows in the DuckDB source used by the most recent fit. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_rows]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Populated by `fit()` via `_count_rows`, which runs a `SELECT COUNT(*)` against the normalized source query before streaming the data. Remains `0` until `fit()` has been called at least once. ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the GAM by reading data from DuckDB.
fit_query() Fit the GAM from an explicit SQL query.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the GAM by reading data from DuckDB. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/duckdb.py#L208-L292){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(source, conn, *, smoothing_params=None, method="fREML", select=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Data is streamed in Arrow batches of `chunk_size` rows (see `_stream_as_dict`), then discretized and fit using the `BigGAM` approach (`build_discretized_model_matrix` + `bam_fit`). The full design matrix is never materialized. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : DuckDB table or view name, or a full `SELECT` query. A bare name such as `"my_table"` is normalized by `_normalize_source` into `"SELECT * FROM my_table"`; a string that already starts with `SELECT` (case-insensitive) is used as-is, e.g. `"SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE year > 2020"`. Any query DuckDB can execute is accepted, including joins, aggregations, and window functions, as long as its output columns cover every variable referenced by `formula`. [conn]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A live DuckDB connection (as returned by `duckdb.connect()`) against which `data` is resolved. The connection must remain open for the duration of `fit()`; it is not closed or modified by this method beyond issuing read queries. [smoothing_params]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list of float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed smoothing parameters. If `None`, selected automatically. [method]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["fREML"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smoothing selection method: `"fREML"` (default), `"REML"`, `"ML"`, or `"GCV"`. [select]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, enable double-penalty variable selection. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DuckDBGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. ::: #### Notes {.doc-notes} When `data` is unambiguously a SQL query rather than a table/view name, `fit_query()` is a thin, more explicit alias for this method. ### [fit_query()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the GAM from an explicit SQL query. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/duckdb.py#L294-L322){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit_query(query, conn, **kwargs) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Equivalent to calling `fit(query, conn, ...)` directly; this method exists purely to document intent at the call site when `source` is unambiguously a SQL query (e.g. one with a `WHERE`, `JOIN`, or aggregation) rather than a bare table or view name. ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [query]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A full `SELECT` query, e.g. `"SELECT * FROM my_table WHERE year > 2020"`. Its output columns must cover every variable referenced by `formula`. [conn]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A live DuckDB connection against which `query` is executed. [**kwargs]{.doc-parameter-name} : Additional keyword arguments forwarded to `fit()`: `smoothing_params`, `method`, and `select`. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DuckDBGAM]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns `self` for method chaining. :::
